 J U D G M E N T

The PSI has submitted charge sheet against the accused for the offence punishable U/s.498A, 323,
324, 307, 504, 506 of IPC in Crime No.35/2022 of Bommanahalli P.S.
2.

The brief story of the prosecution are as under:

1
The marriage between the accused and complainant performed on 13.11.2005.
After marriage, they started to reside in the second floor situated at Rajendra building, 2 nd cross, Hongasandra, within the limits of Bommanahalli police station.
Due to the marital relationship, the complainant gave birth to a son and daughter by name Aishwarya and Rakesh respectively.
Such being the case, the accused is in the habit of consuming alcohol.
Due to the addiction for consuming of liquor, the accused everyday after returning home in intoxication condition and forcing and demanding the complainant to give money to fulfill his bad habits.
The accused not spending any amount towards the maintenance of the family nor paying the money towards the education of his children etc.
The accused used to assault the complainant by abusing in filthy language and thereby harassing the complainant physically and mentally.

On 09.03.2022 at 2.00 p.m, the accused suspected the fidelity of the complainant and picked up quarrel for not giving money to consume liquor and because of that reason,
the accused abused the complainant in filthy language and with an intention to kill the complainant given a fist blow on her face and dragged by holding her tuft and pushed the complainant on ground.

When the complainant tried to escape and want to come outside of the house, at that time, the accused brought the machete from the kitchen with an intention to kill the complainant and thereby the accused has committed the offences as alleged against him.
3. The concerned police have submitted charge sheet before the concerned ACMM., Bangalore.
The learned Magistrate has took cognizance of the offences and committed the case to the Sessions Court by complying Sec.207 of Cr.P.C. after furnishing copy of charge sheet to the accused.
The same was numbered as SC No.1137/2022.
4. The prosecution has examined ten witnesses as PW.1 to PW.10 and got exhibited documents at Ex.P1 to P8.
The witnesses C.W.3 and C.W12 remained absent before the court.
Inspite of issue of summons, bailable warrant and NBW the concerned police failed to execute the same and keep them present before the court.
As such the prayer of the learned public prosecutor was rejected and the witnesses C.W.3 and C.W.12 were dropped.
5. The accused has pleaded not guilty.
After completion of prosecution side evidence, this Court has recorded the statement of accused, as provided U/s.313 of Cr.P.C.
The accused has denied incriminating evidence present against him and not claimed any defense evidence nor submitted anything to the Court.
The accused has complied application u/s.437A of Cr.PC by executing personal bond and surety bond.

6. Heard the arguments on both sides and perused the materials on record.
7.

The following points that arises for consideration of this court:
1. Whether the prosecution proves that the marriage of accused with the C.W.1 Rukmini was solemnized on 13.11.2005 and started to reside in a rented house of Rajendra building at 2nd floor, 2nd cross, Shanthinagar, Hongasandra, within the Bommanahalli P.S vs Ravi on 3 January, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/64200871/
2 limits of Bommanahalli police station, the accused being the husband of C.W.1 Rukmini consumed alcohol and was not providing amount for household articles and for education of children and used to abuse and assault her and subjected her to physical and mental cruelty and thereby the accused has committed offence punishable U/s.498A of IPC?
2.

Whether the prosecution proves that on 09.03.2022 at 2.00 p.m accused quarreled with C.W.1 and suspecting her fidelity and abused her in filthy language knowingly that such provocation will cause the said person to break the public peace and thereby accused has committed an offence punishable under section 504 of IPC?

3. Whether the prosecution proves that on 09.03.2022 at 2.00 p.m accused quarreled with C.W.1 and suspecting her fidelity and caused criminal intimidation to her by threatening her that he will finish her & thereby accused has committed an offence punishable under Section 506 of IPC?

4. Whether the prosecution proves that on 09.03.2022 at 2.00 p.m accused quarreled with C.W.1 and suspecting her fidelity assaulted her with hands on her face and by holding her tuft dragged her and pushed her head to the wall and gave a flush blow on her cheek and thereby committed the offence punishable u/s 323 of IPC?

5. Whether the prosecution proves that on 09.03.2022 at 2.00 p.m accused quarreled with C.W.1 and suspecting her fidelity attempted to assault her with machete kept in the kitchen and thereby committed the offence punishable u/s 324 of IPC?

6. Whether the prosecution proves that on 09.03.2022 at 2.00 p.m accused quarreled with C.W.1 and suspecting her fidelity, accused with an intention and knowledge to kill C.W.1 attempted to assault the CW.1 with machete kept in the kitchen and thereby accused has committed an offence punishable U/s.307 of IPC?
7. What order?

sentences.text: Points Nos.1 to 6: These points are taken up together as they are related to each other and to avoid repetition in the discussion.

The prosecution got examined prime witness of the prosecution and victim by name Rukmini ie.
complainant as P.W.2.
Admittedly, the complainant is none other than the wife of the accused.
According to the evidence of complainant, the accused is an Electrician and she was working in the garments.
Due to the marital relationship, they are having two children.
The further evidence of complainant reveals that the accused is in the habit of consuming liquor and used to quarrel for silly reasons.
Because of that, when she went to the police station, the police instructed to settle the dispute between themselves.
Except that no any acceptable evidence deposed by the complainant.
According to the complainant, the accused never tried to assault with a machete and she has not taken any treatment in the hospital.
Even today, she and accused alongwith their children residing happily.
Though the complaint has been marked through this witness as Ex.P.2, but it is the specific say of the complainant that the accused never tried to kill her.

Since the evidence of the complainant went against to the recitals of the complaint and prosecution story, hence learned PP has treated the said witness as hostile and cross-examined with the permission of the court by suggesting the incriminating evidence present in the complaint and charge.
But the complainant has not admitted any suggestions of the learned PP.
As such the evidence of the wife of the complainant by name Rukmini not worthful to believe the allegations made against the accused.
10. The family relatives by name Kumar, Manjula, Krishna and another Kumar have been examined by the prosecution as PW.4 to P.W.7 respectively.

According to the evidence of the said witness P.W.4 to P.W.7, the accused never tortured the complainant either physically or mentally for any reasons nor abused and given threat to her life and never tried to kill the complainant by using machete.
According to these witnesses the police have not recorded their respective statements.
The said witnesses including the complainant not identified the machete present before the court.
Since the evidence of said witnesses contrary to the story of the prosecution, hence the learned PP has treated the said witnesses as hostile with the permission of the court and cross-examined.
The prosecution has failed to elicit any incriminating evidence during the cross- examination of the said witnesses to believe the allegation made against the accused.
As such the evidence by P.W.4 to P.W.7 not helpful for the prosecution to prove the guilt against the accused.
11. It is necessary to note that the owner of the house by name Sujatha also not supported the prosecution story.
According to the evidence of P.W.3 Sujatha, the accused and complainant residing in their house since 9 years on the basis of mortgage.

There is no any quarrel between the accused and complainant for any reasons and the accused never harassed the complainant physically or mentally by abusing in filthy language by giving threat to her life and assaulted the complainant with hands and brought a machete with an intention to kill the complainant.

So also,
the sole pancha examined by the prosecution by name Mohan Kumar as P.W.1 failed to support the contents of the panchanama marked at Ex.P.1.
According to the said witness P.W.1, the police have obtained the signature about 2 or 3 years back in the police station.

Though he has identified the document Mahazar and his signature present on it, but failed to depose anything with regard to Bommanahalli P.S vs Ravi on 3 January, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/64200871/
4 mahazar nor identified his machete.
The said witness further not supported the prosecution by saying machete was not seized in his presence.

As such, the learned PP has treated the said witnesses P.W.3 and P.W.1 as hostile and cross-examined, but failed to get any useful evidence to prove the contents of the statement of P.W.3 and recitals of the Mahazar Ex.P.1.
As such, the evidence of the witnesses P.W.3 and P.W.1 are not helpful for the prosecution in any angle.
So, it is very clear from the above discussions that none of the independent witness including the victim not supported the prosecution story and also did not identified the machete.
12. In this case, the prosecution examined the Doctor Ashwath Narayana i.e. C.W.9 as P.W.8.
It is very clear from the evidence of the said doctor that on 10.03.2022 at 1.10 p.m., the complainant came to hospital with history of assault.
He has treated the victim and issued wound certificate as per Ex.P.8.
According to the doctor, there was contusion on her right cheek, abrasion present on right ring finger and contusion on right scapular area of the complainant.
The said evidence of the doctor has completely denied by the accused counsel.

13. The police witness by name Devareddappa examined as P.W.9, who has registered FIR on the basis of the complaint lodged by the complainant on 09.03.2022 as per FIR No.35/2022 and thereafter handed over further investigation to C.W.12.
The another police witness by name Chethan Kumar.D.S examined as P.W.10 being the PSI has collected wound certificate Ex.P.8 of the victim and submitted charge sheet against the accused.
The evidence given by the said police witness completely denied by the accused counsel.

In this case, the another prime witness C.W.12 by name Anand.H.M, PSI being the Investigation Officer of this case has failed to appear before the court inspite of issue of summons, bailable warrant and warrant.
So, the said witness was dropped.
Due to the absence of the said witness, the prosecution unable to examine the Investigation Officer who has carried out major investigation of this case.

Even if assumed that the said Investigation Officer has appeared and given evidence according to his investigation, perhaps as already discussed above, the prime witness i.e victim and all other independent witnesses including pancha were turned hostile and thereby supported the prosecution story.
As such, much importance could not have been given to the evidence of this Investigation Officer C.W.12 even if his evidence present on record.
So, it is very clear from the above discussions that the prosecution has completely failed to place the reliable iota evidence before the court to prove the allegations made against the accused.
As such, this court has answered the Point Nos.1 to 6 in the Negative.
14. Point No.7:

In view of answer of this court on points No.1 to 6, this court proceed to pass the following:
O R D E R U/s.235(1) of Cr.P.C. the accused is hereby acquitted of the offences punishable under Sections 498A, 323, 324, 307, 504, 506 of IPC.
The bail bond and surety bond of accused stands cancelled.
The M.O.1 is Machete being worthful shall be confiscated to State as per law after expiry of appeal time.
